title: The Secret Group Chat
premise: Marguerite Eriksen has survived two years at Ashford Academy by being invisible — until her economics teacher pairs her with Callum Reyes, the popular athlete whose friends made her life hell, for a semester project auditing the school's scholarship fund. Digging through ledgers, they discover the 'Secret Group Chat': a thread where wealthy parents and administrators trade grades, silence, and scholarship slots like currency, including the slot that was supposed to be Marguerite's. As Marguerite and Callum fall for each other across enemy lines, she must choose between exposing the chat and losing everything — or staying quiet and keeping the fragile life she's built. At the season's final game, she goes public in front of the whole school, trading her scholarship for justice, and finds that the family she chose is worth more than the one that bought her seat.
about_author: Sable Iversen grew up bouncing between public schools and a prestigious academy on financial aid, an experience that taught her how institutions protect themselves and how students survive them anyway. She writes young adult fiction about outsiders who refuse to stay quiet, from a small apartment full of plants and half-finished manuscripts.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We meet her rules of survival at Ashford: never draw attention, never owe anyone, never let them see you need the scholarship. When her locker is vandalized with 'charity case,' she cleans it alone rather than report it. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as control.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Ms. Okafor pairs her with Callum Reyes to audit the school's endowment spending — a project worth half their grade. Their first meeting is ice; his friends snicker in the background. Marguerite resolves to do all the work herself. Emotional beat: resentment hardening into armor.

chapters.title: Numbers Don't Flatter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced together in the library, they find discrepancies: funds earmarked for scholarships flowing into vague 'development' accounts. Callum, surprisingly sharp with spreadsheets, notices what Marguerite missed. A grudging truce forms over takeout fries. Emotional beat: the first crack in the nemesis narrative.

chapters.title: The Thread
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Borrowing his teammate's laptop, Callum glimpses a group chat he was never meant to see — parents and administrators discussing 'slots.' He recognizes his own father's handle. Shaken, he tells Marguerite only part of it. Emotional beat: loyalty to family colliding with conscience.

chapters.title: What Her Slot Cost
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They trace the money and find the truth: Marguerite's scholarship was real once — until it was quietly reassigned to a donor's son, with a lesser 'pity' package created as cover. Marguerite realizes her entire Ashford life was built on someone else's theft. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Working late, the walls come down — a near-kiss interrupted by Callum's teammates, who mock Marguerite within earshot. Callum doesn't defend her fast enough. She walks out. Meanwhile, someone notices their audit queries in the school system logs. Emotional beat: tenderness sabotaged by old habits; danger stirring.

chapters.title: Leverage
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. The headmaster privately warns Callum about his college recommendations and his father's business ties, making clear the project should 'conclude cleanly.' Callum must decide whose side he's on. He copies the chat archives onto a drive. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite is accused of hacking the school records and suspended pending expulsion — the machine protecting itself. Callum publicly breaks with his friends and hands Ms. Okafor the drive, but the board buries it. Emotional beat: betrayal at its peak, and the cost of doing right becoming real.

chapters.title: The Last Game
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Championship night, packed stadium, trustees in the stands. During halftime, Marguerite takes the mic during the scholar-athlete ceremony and reads the chat aloud, message by message, while Callum holds the crowd's phones aloft streaming it live. Emotional beat: terror becoming triumph; love declared in action, not words.

chapters.title: Labels Off
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Aftermath: resignations, an investigation, Callum's father facing consequences, and Marguerite expelled but offered a full ride elsewhere — plus a journalism mentorship from a reporter who saw the stream. She and Callum choose each other without the school between them. Emotional beat: bittersweet victory; survival redefined as living truthfully.
